text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli army nabs riot leaders. Undercover troops in Hebron infiltrate stone-throwers.
- Sephardi Chief Rabbi Eliahu Bakshi-Doron meets Hebron mufti, tells him pig poster was disgusting.
- Tel Aviv cafe bomber escapes from Palestinian Authority jail.
- Bezeq workers yield, hook up phone competitors.
- Koor postponed Yankee bond issue due to differences with Shamrock.
- 600 million shekels budget cut due soon -- prime minister's office.
- Merhav group: Egypt-Israel oil project launched.
GLOBES
- Dollar devalued 0.34 percent to 3.517 shekels.
- Treasury decides to sign wage pacts for two years from now on instead of for four years.
HAARETZ
- Israeli effort to pressure the Palestinian Authority into preventing violence in territories.
- Israel agrees to establish diplomatic ties with Croatia.
- Israeli President Ezer Weizman believes 2.9-million-shekel renovation of prime minister's airforce plane was unnecessary.
MAARIV
- Businessmen close to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu conduct secret contacts with Syrian President Hafez al-Assad but so far no formula has been found for renewing negotiations.
- U.N. Secretary General says he hopes there will be no need for sanctions in dealing with Arab-Israeli conflict.
- Netanyahu to Japan at end of August.
- Increased alert in Hebron.

- Gallup poll shows 57 percent of Israelis believe Foreign Minister David Levy threatened to quit out of concern for honour and personal worth rather than real issues while 55 percent believe the media treat Netanyahu's wife unfairly.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Tension in Hebron: fear of demonstrations at end of Friday prayers.
- Revolution in international phone calls begins.
- Participant in killing of two Palestinians captured in Bus 300 episode is security adviser to all official institutions.
